video.title: Coiling | Spinal Motion | Eye Dominance | Arm Slot - 15 Serves Explained

classification.reason: The coach analyzes slow-motion footage of professional serves to explain core mechanics, anatomical constraints, ocular dominance, and actionable techniques for recreational players.

problem.title_as_question: How should you tailor your serve mechanics to your personal anatomy, spinal mobility, and eye dominance?
problem.definition: Many players blindly copy aesthetically pleasing pro motions like Federer's without accounting for eye dominance, leading to lost court awareness, misaligned arm slots, and poor rotational power from the trunk and shoulder.
prerequisites: Basic understanding of continental serve motion
Ability to toss and strike an overhead serve
problem.target_player: Players struggling with serve velocity, accuracy, or copying pro serves that feel awkward

quotes.text: The first is coiling. And when we say coiling, what we mean is stretching the off shoulder against the hitting side hip.
quotes.speaker: coach

quotes.text: Elbow and shoulder down and back. Elbow and shoulder down and back. So what we have here, we have the opposite. Here we're stretched in the back. Here we're stretched in the front.
quotes.speaker: coach

quotes.text: So see how the spine is curved back. The top of the spine is curved back here. Again, not every player can do this, but Shelton can.
quotes.speaker: coach

quotes.text: arm slot, absolute arm slot with respect to the ground is not as important as keeping your arm in the same plane of rotation as your shoulders.
quotes.speaker: coach

quotes.text: If you pronate, great. If you don't pronate, it's not that big of a deal. What I want you to notice with pistol P. The shoulder drives serve velocity.
quotes.speaker: coach

quotes.text: Because it was stretched backwards, it internally rotates forcibly reactively through the hitting zone. Shoulder rotation is what drives serve velocity.
quotes.speaker: coach

quotes.text: And I think, ironically enough, Federer looking so good serving with this technique has actually created a lot of issues for players trying to learn the serve.
quotes.speaker: coach

quotes.text: If you can't see the service box, your aim is going to be way, way worse. And if you can't see your opponent, you're never going to know when they cheat on your serve.
quotes.speaker: coach

quotes.text: The upshot here, you cannot copy a player's loading phase if you have the opposite eye dominance that they have because it will not work.
quotes.speaker: coach

quotes.text: When you're right eye dominant, you just need to keep everything facing forward more. But in order to power your serve, you must rotate.
quotes.speaker: coach

quotes.text: And so the only way to to meet both of those criteria is to allow yourself to fall off to the left and rotate.
quotes.speaker: coach

quotes.text: And if you've never felt this, if you're a right eye dominant player and you've never felt this, you've got to try serving more forward. All of a sudden, your accuracy is going to go way up.
quotes.speaker: coach

quotes.text: Now, Yakob Mezv uses my favorite technique for the right eye dominant server, which is what I call the purodextral pinpoint. And I want you to look at the way he does this pinpoint.
quotes.speaker: coach

quotes.text: If you're already serving pinpoint and you're right eye dominant, try this pinpoint because you're going to be able to coil your shoulder against your hip a lot more without having to turn so far away from the court.
quotes.speaker: coach

quotes.text: This you you lose such a tiny amount of power, but you completely protect your elbow against hyperextension. So don't think that your arm has to straighten out.
quotes.speaker: coach

quotes.text: And you are going to get much bigger bang for your buck by working on your upper body than you are by trying to use your legs.
quotes.speaker: coach

quotes.text: See where the hand is being thrown. See how the hand is being thrown towards the ad side service box and then internal shoulder rotation will cause the racket to send the ball to your left.
quotes.speaker: coach

quotes.text: I want to work on one of the cues that I find helps people really get there and it's to throw your chest to the sky.
quotes.speaker: coach

quotes.text: If you rotate, you're not twisting forward. You're twisting diagonally up and forward.
quotes.speaker: coach

quotes.text: Alexis preparation is one that you can copy if you're struggling with the early rhythm. Just take your arm, put it back in the 9090 position. Very simple, just place it there.
quotes.speaker: coach

quotes.text: And this where you finish, you land, you get wide, you split, and then you react and you track and receive that first ball. that has to be seamlessly integrated into the service process
quotes.speaker: coach

symptoms.description: Serve aim is inaccurate and the player is unaware of opponent repositioning during toss and loading.
Right-eye dominant server falls to the left during and immediately after the forward swing.
Severe loss of serve velocity when the hitting arm is elevated vertically out of plane with level shoulders.

causes.statement: The hitting arm is raised independently without sufficient shoulder tilt, pulling it out of the shoulders' plane of rotation.
Players attempt to generate serve velocity primarily through forearm pronation or leg push rather than reactive trunk and shoulder internal rotation.
Right-eye dominant players copy cross-dextral coil positions, blinding their dominant back eye from tracking the court in peripheral vision.
Right-eye dominant servers must keep the torso more forward to maintain peripheral vision while still rotating forcefully into the ball.

angles.summary: Serve power originates from stretching the off shoulder against the back hip and spring-loading the trunk through thoracic extension and shoulder external rotation.
Forearm pronation and leg drive are heavily overrated for velocity compared to trunk spring-loading and reactive internal shoulder rotation.
Federer can coil deeply because his court-facing left eye is dominant, allowing peripheral court tracking that right-eye dominant players cannot replicate.
Serving is felt as an upward throwing motion where the chest fires to the sky rather than twisting flat toward the net.

solutions.summary: If right-eye dominant, keep your head and chest facing more forward so your back eye retains peripheral vision of the court.
solutions.external_goal: Keep the service box visible in your peripheral vision during preparation.

solutions.summary: Use the pure-dextral pinpoint by stepping the back foot onto the hitting side of the off foot to achieve coil without over-turning the torso away from the court.
solutions.external_goal: Step back foot onto the hitting side of front foot into an open-stance base.

solutions.summary: Throw your hitting hand toward the center of the opposite service box and let reactive shoulder internal rotation direct the ball.
solutions.external_goal: Center of the ad-side service box (for a right-hander).

solutions.summary: Throw your chest to the sky during upward drive rather than rotating flat toward the net.
Simplify preparation by pre-placing the hitting arm directly into the 90-90 position to bypass early rhythm and timing problems.
Integrate the serve finish immediately into landing wide, split-stepping, and tracking the incoming return ball.
solutions.external_goal: The incoming return ball across the net.
